profile.name: Frigate Bird Dance (Nauru)
profile.tagline: A surviving contemporary Nauruan dance echoing avian traditions.
profile.insight: On an island where traditional arts were largely eroded by colonial influence, the frigate bird dance endures as a rare named performance.
profile.profile: The Frigate Bird Dance is a known contemporary dance of Nauru, practiced alongside rhythmic singing and traditional reigen. While much of Nauru's traditional culture has given way to contemporary Western influences, music and dance remain vital. Alongside the dogoropa, this performance art preserves a fragment of indigenous movement.
profile.profile_long: The displacement of the traditional culture of Nauru by contemporary Western influences is evident across the island, leaving little of the old customs intact. Despite this cultural erosion, music and dance still rank among the most popular art forms practiced by the inhabitants. Alongside the dogoropa, the frigate bird dance stands out as a known contemporary dance form, contrasting with historical practices like the fish dance that survive only in photographs. Rhythmic singing and traditional reigen accompany these occasions, performed particularly at celebrations. Historically, Nauruans participated in indigenous dances that were heavily discouraged or altered by European contact, wearing coconut leaf skirts known as ridis and body oils before shifting toward standard tropical attire such as short trousers and light shirts.

sections.origins_and_history: The displacement of the traditional culture of Nauru by contemporary Western influences is evident on the island. Little remains from the old customs, and traditions of arts and crafts are nearly lost. Known contemporary dances include the frigate bird dance and the dogoropa, alongside a historical form of a Nauruan fish dance recorded only in photographs.
sections.music_and_instruments: Rhythmic singing accompanies traditional performances and reigen on the island, particularly at celebrations.
sections.costume_and_setting: Inhabitants of Nauru wear standard tropical clothes, including short trousers and light shirts. Historically, Nauruans wore skirts made from coconut leaves, known as ridis, and rubbed their bodies with coconut oil before these customs were largely replaced.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Rhythmic singing and traditional reigen are performed particularly at celebrations, reflecting the enduring popularity of music and dance despite widespread cultural displacement.
sections.lineage: Connected to Nauruan performance traditions, alongside the dogoropa and the historical fish dance.
